court: District Court of Appeal of Florida

issues.label: Alimony entitlement and need/ability to pay
issues.why: Court must determine whether alimony is warranted based on the Former Wife's need and the Former Husband's ability to pay.

issues.label: Statutory alimony factors including marriage length
issues.why: A 26-year marriage triggers durational alimony analysis and required statutory factor findings under Florida law.

issues.label: Sufficiency of alimony findings
issues.why: The court must make adequate factual findings supporting the type, amount, and duration of alimony awarded.

issues.label: Propriety of lump sum durational alimony
issues.why: Whether lump sum durational alimony is a legally permissible and supported form of award must be assessed.

issues.label: Child support amount calculation
issues.why: Court must verify the guidelines calculation and income figures producing the $1,344 support figure.

issues.label: Retroactive child support to separation date
issues.why: Whether support may be made retroactive to separation and how far back it may reach must be determined.

issues.label: Credit for temporary support overage
issues.why: Court must account for the Former Husband's prior $1,500 temporary payments and any overage credited against arrears.

issues.label: Imputation and income determination
issues.why: Each party's actual or imputable income affects both support and alimony calculations.

issues.label: Equitable distribution of $5M assets
issues.why: Court must classify and equitably distribute the substantial marital estate.

issues.label: Classification of separate vs marital accounts
issues.why: The parties' separate and joint accounts require characterization as marital or nonmarital property.

issues.label: Date of valuation and separation
issues.why: June 20, 2022 separation date affects asset valuation and distribution cutoffs.

issues.label: Unpaid household/child expenses credit
issues.why: The Former Wife's $13,000 expenditures and Husband's stopped contributions may warrant reimbursement or credit.

issues.label: HSA and health care contributions
issues.why: Failure to contribute to the HSA and child healthcare may factor into support and equitable distribution.

issues.label: Health insurance and uncovered medical costs
issues.why: Allocation of the child's medical expenses and insurance obligations must be addressed.

issues.label: Ultimate decision-making authority award
issues.why: Court must justify granting the Former Wife sole ultimate decision-making under best-interests standard.

issues.label: Best interests and parenting plan
issues.why: Time-sharing and parenting responsibilities for the minor child require best-interests analysis.

issues.label: Child support duration until majority
issues.why: Whether support properly continues to majority, including any high-school extension, must be confirmed.

issues.label: Preservation without motion for rehearing
issues.why: Absence of a rehearing motion may waive challenges to the judgment's factual findings on appeal.

issues.label: Tax consequences of awards
issues.why: Tax treatment of alimony, support, and asset transfers may affect the fairness of allocations.

issues.label: Credibility of conflicting expense testimony
issues.why: Court must resolve disputed testimony about sufficiency of joint contributions and expense coverage.
